dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It seems we have a third contestant who has returned with a Swiftfly.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: With that, the first round has come to an end. I anticipate that all of you will keep up the effort for the second round. Dismissed.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Ah, um... Your closing statement sounded so... How do I put it... Decisive?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Well, you could certainly stand to try being more decisive, Nilou. It would help you live more freely.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hang on a second! Who were the first two contestants with Swiftflies?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Tighnari was first, and as for the second... It's being discussed right now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's being discussed?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hey, Alhaitham, I think I've come up with a good idea.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Second place gets two points, right? Can't Madam Faruzan and I split the points between us?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Quite the imagination you have there. I've read the Championship handbook from cover to cover, and I never saw any rule which permits that.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Then we can just add a rule.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Do you really think I'd do that?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: C'mon, you're not going to stand in the way of my victory, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Well, you're free to send the organizing committee an application outlining your naive proposal. They'll get back to you within three working days.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Three working days? It'll be too late by then!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Unfortunately for you, even dreaming is gonna cost you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, Paimon gets it now. Kaveh and Faruzan found the second Swiftfly together, but the rules say that only one person can get the points...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Ah well, the rules are the rules. Since you call me "Madam" and politely asked for my help, I shall give you these points.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: So I'll put the points under Kaveh's name, then?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: No. If I take these points, won't that only detract from your contributions, Madam Faruzan?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You might be alright with that, but I cannot do it, not in good conscience.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: I don't have any problem with it. There are two more rounds, after all. Losing one isn't a major setback.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: But if you insist, I have another method — we can draw lots to see who will receive the points.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: L—Lots, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: What? Is there something wrong with that idea?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...No. Let's do it.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Alright, I'll get the paper needed for the lots. Give me a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Everybody watches Kaveh suffer a glorious and forthright defeat in the game of lots.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Ugh, seriously...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, but it appears that luck was on my side this time.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: No, you do deserve it... I'm just lamenting my bad luck. Perhaps... *sigh* Perhaps that's why my life is rife with troubles...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Indeed, it's rare to see anyone with such terrible luck be so willing to decide victory via lots.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: And what would you know about that? I just...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: We can save bickering for later. Record the points under Faruzan, and that'll finally bring the first round to a close.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The second round will be held in the desert. We'll be moving our commentator's stand over to Aaru Village.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Let's meet up in Aaru Village once everything is ready. I'll announce the details of the second round then.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Till then, you have some free time. I'm off the clock at this point, so it's farewell for now.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Wait, Alhaitham! You...! *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Don't be upset, Kaveh. Sighing can carry away your good luck, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, so that's how it works? In that case, I'll take in some deep breaths. Maybe that'll help make up for all the luck I've lost!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: *deep breath* It's really no big deal. Two points aren't enough to decide victory or defeat just yet.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I'll win the next round, you'll see!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Looks like you've managed to pick yourself back up, young man. Good. I must warn you, though, that I'm quite familiar with the desert. You'll have to try your best if you don't want to lose.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I'm no stranger to the desert either, I'll be fine. Alright then, that's enough chit-chat for now. I'm going to check the area out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... So the current standings are Tighnari in first place, Faruzan in second, and Layla in third.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess we should also take a nice break before the next round starts. But where should we go first?

dialogues.speaker: Morgiana
dialogues.text: Why, you two look a little lost. If you're not sure where to start enjoying the Akademiya Extravaganza, then may I suggest that you have a chat with our boss?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your boss? Who's that? Do we know them?

dialogues.speaker: Morgiana
dialogues.text: Hehe, well, only the most famous merchant in all of Sumeru — Lord Sangemah Bay!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean Dori!

dialogues.speaker: Morgiana
dialogues.text: Precisely! Our boss sent me to inform you two that she'll be waiting for you at Sumeru City's north gate.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Looks like the second round is over. I wonder who was faster, Kaveh or Madam Faruzan? ...Huh? Where's Madam Faruzan?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: She went to get water — she'll be back shortly. We basically arrived at the same time, so we'd like to draw lots again.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You get caught up in some things so easily — like drawing lots.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I'm not "caught up" in anything! Don't make it sound like I take pleasure in having bad luck!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Really? Then, should I say that you have a curious affinity for drawing lots?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Um, I'll go get the box and slips of paper for the lots. Please wait a moment...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Oho, here we go again. Let's see how I fare.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After a brief but tense lot-drawing, Kaveh emerges triumphant...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I got it! Did you see that? I won!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Congratulations!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like Kaveh's luck's taken a turn for the better!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Finally, after all this time... *sniff*

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: It looks like you've been rewarded for your tribulations in the desert. This round's points are yours.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: And with that, our second round is done. Cyno, Layla, and Kaveh are our victorious contestants!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: As for the current standings, let me see...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Cyno and Layla both have four points, putting them both in first place. The rest in descending order are Tighnari, Faruzan, Kaveh, and Hat Guy.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: The next round will be the final one. Please rest up before then, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: I heard that some stalls at the Wisdom Gala are debuting new games, so feel free to drop by if you're interested. Otherwise, see you next round!

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: ...Thank you all for your excellent performance. And that brings this year's Interdarshan Championship to a close!

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Finally, it gives me great pleasure to invite our champion, Kaveh, to the stage to receive his award.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Typically, at this point, we would crown our champion with the diadem as well as presenting them with their award.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: However, we have just received word that Kaveh has inherited Sachin's estate, and made the decision to donate it all to charitable causes.

dialogues.speaker: Marwa
dialogues.text: Sachin's estate... is getting donated?

dialogues.speaker: Alae
dialogues.text: So much Mora... and he gave it all up?

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Kaveh's generosity will give many struggling families the chance to change their lives for the better.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Of course, without the diadem and prize money to present, this makes the award ceremony a little more concise than expected. Would you like to say a few words, Kaveh? I'm sure many of our audience, like myself, are curious to learn why you decided to give all this wealth away.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I'm... not entirely sure what I should say under these circumstances. I'm glad to have won, even though I'd say luck played a big part in that.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: As for why I want to give the Mora away... I don't support Sachin's views, and I don't want to take his Mora. With a lot of things in life, people need to experience them for themselves. It shouldn't be up to one person to make a judgment on — not him, and not me either.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Anyway, this isn't really the time and place for such weighty and complicated topics. So umm... I guess that's all. I'll leave it there, thanks very much.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Oh, Kaveh... just one moment.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: While this is a short-and-sweet award ceremony, we do still have a prize to present you with. Please take this limited-edition Genius Invokation TCG card.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: Additionally, your champion status will be logged in your record. This means that the sages will give priority consideration to any future project proposals you submit.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Alright, I'll take the card. But as for project proposals... Eh, forget it.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: In that case, I declare the award ceremony over. Let's give our champion, Kaveh one last big round of applause!

dialogues.speaker: Aissa
dialogues.text: I still don't really get it. That sum of Mora would've been enough for me to live in luxury for my entire life.

dialogues.speaker: Bahir
dialogues.text: That just means you're not strange enough to understand the way that geniuses think. Come on, we've still got the whole Wisdom Gala to explore!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: *sigh* Glad that's over. I think I'm quite good at giving speeches, but this one was just so tiring...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you mean that you're still exhausted from the competition? Honestly, you don't look happy at all... But whatever else happened, you're the champion, you know? Don't you think you should be proud of that?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I suppose... *sigh* Oh, wait. Cyno said that he wanted the card, didn't he? And now I have it, right here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you're gonna give it to him? But, if it's a rare one, you should be able to make a tidy sum of Mora off it!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Why would I do that? It's of no use to me whatsoever — I may as well just give it to him. Could you pass it on to him for me when you next see him?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, whoa, this is a super big deal. You should do it yourself! Come on, let's go find Cyno!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Huh? But I was gonna rest for a while longer— hey, hey, stop pulling my hair!
